newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar slightly weaker in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar slightly weaker in thin trade.

text.p: London's white sugar futures market got off to a slow start on Thursday with the spot October contract dominating the morning's thin activity, traders said.
By 1145 GMT October stood just 50 cents lower at $327.50 and comprised the vast majority of the total 497 lots traded. December was down 30 cents at $321.70.
Technical analysts said October's overbought condition could be safely ignored for the time being, pegging nearby resistance at $335 and slightly above.

On the fundamental side, traders said the market's high levels were deterring destination sales. Syria has retendered to buy 13,000 tonnes of white sugar and 13,000 tonnes of raws with the deadline set for August 5.
The two amounts should be shipped in September.
The Paris market was quiet with just 144 lots posted on the board. October was up 50 cents at $327.50 and December down 20 cents at $321.80.
Five lots of front October were traded on the lesser-quality 100 ICUMSA market. The contract was flat at $301.40.
